name: AI Job Guide / 01 Job Ingestion
description: Manual trigger, dryRun-default job ingestion. n8n owns provider HTTP fetch/retry/rate-limiting for sources discovered dynamically from company_sources (Phase 12) across three tiers (Phase 13): company-specific ATS, multi-company feeds, career-page extraction. TypeScript owns validation, dedup, persistence via three internal endpoints.

nodes.name: List Ingestion Sources
nodes.notes: Discovers verified, automatable company_sources rows dynamically (Phase 12), plus enabled multi-company feed providers and career-page extraction candidates (Phase 13). See src/lib/ingestion/findEligibleCompanySources.ts, multiCompanyFeedUrls.ts, findCareerPageExtractionCandidates.ts.

nodes.name: Log List Sources Failure
nodes.notes: Terminal failure for this run — nothing to loop over if source discovery itself failed. A human reviews the n8n execution log.

nodes.name: Aggregate Lever Jobs
nodes.notes: Phase 14 fix. Lever's postings API returns a bare top-level JSON array, so n8n's core JSON-to-items conversion auto-splits it into one item per job (confirmed live: a real 21-job response from Wahed's board produced 21 separate items reaching this branch, each individually failing Extract Lever Jobs's old 'rawJobs: $json' assumption that $json was still the whole array). Collects them back into one {jobs:[...]} item first, mirroring the same pattern already used for RemoteOK in the Tier-D branch below.

nodes.name: Extract Lever Jobs
nodes.notes: Lever's postings API returns a bare top-level array, auto-split by n8n into one item per job — Aggregate Lever Jobs collects them back into a single {jobs:[...]} item before this node runs (Phase 14 fix; docs/job-ingestion-pilot.md §5).

nodes.name: Extract Ashby Jobs
nodes.notes: Phase 13. Ashby posting-api returns {jobs:[...], apiVersion} — confirmed live against a real registry board (sr-qa-the-utopia-studio).

nodes.name: Prepare Oracle HCM Page State
nodes.notes: 2026-10-23 pagination-safety phase. Classifies the FIRST page (already fetched by the shared Fetch Source Jobs node) using only the response's own items[0].{Offset,Limit,TotalJobsCount,requisitionList} — never the requested limit=50. A malformed/unparseable response, or a merge that fails its own integrity check, fails closed (paginationIncomplete:true, zero jobs accumulated). Mirrors classifyOracleHcmFirstPage in src/lib/ingestion/oracleHcmPagination.ts exactly. 2026-10-24: moved from a Set-node inline expression into a Code node — an isolated n8n diagnostic (executions 300293/300549/300782) proved Array.from(map.values()) and the [...map.values()] spread form both silently return an empty array inside the Set-node inline-expression evaluator despite the Map itself reporting the correct size; the Code node's real JS sandbox does not share that defect. Also throws (routed to its own error output, never silently) if it ever receives more than 1 input item — runOnceForAllItems + $input.first() would otherwise silently discard the rest; the current graph never sends it more than 1 (Loop Sources batchSize=1, no HTTP pagination on Fetch Source Jobs), but this guard makes that invariant fail loud instead of fail silent if it is ever broken.

nodes.name: Check Oracle HCM Page 1 Complete?
nodes.notes: case 0 = already complete (or already known malformed) from page 1 alone — the real, live-tested AUBMC case (8 jobs, one page). Fallback = genuinely needs more pages, enters the bounded loop below.

nodes.name: Fetch Oracle HCM Next Page
nodes.notes: Free, idempotent read — safe to retry. A null nextPageUrl (feed_url shape unrecognized — defensive, never observed live) simply fails this request, which routes through the same error path as any other failure. Both this node's success AND error outputs feed Carry Forward Oracle HCM Page State's second input — pageState itself is recovered from that Merge node's OTHER (untouched) input regardless of which output fires here.

nodes.name: Merge & Classify Oracle HCM Page
nodes.notes: Mirrors classifyOracleHcmNextPage in src/lib/ingestion/oracleHcmPagination.ts (including that module's own 2026-10-24 fix: missing/invalid Ids are never collapsed into each other, and an explicit integrity check fails closed if a merge ever loses a valid Id or returns empty despite non-empty inputs), plus one n8n-specific check the pure module doesn't need (its caller already separates success/failure): input.error, set by Carry Forward Oracle HCM Page State whenever Fetch Oracle HCM Next Page's error output fired. Fails closed on: a fetch failure; malformed metadata; a non-advancing/repeated offset; a premature empty page; or the merge step itself failing its own integrity check. Its own error output is explicitly wired. 2026-10-24: moved from a Set-node inline expression into a Code node for the same reason as Prepare Oracle HCM Page State above — the exact node most at risk, since THIS is the step that actually merges two pages' worth of jobs together. Also throws (routed to its own error output, never silently) if it ever receives more than 1 input item — runOnceForAllItems + $input.first() would otherwise silently discard the rest; the current graph never sends it more than 1 (single-item cycle, Merge combineByPosition pairs exactly 1:1), but this guard makes that invariant fail loud instead of fail silent if it is ever broken.

nodes.name: Route Oracle HCM Page Outcome
nodes.notes: case 0 = genuinely needs another page AND still under the bound (loop back, directly to Prepare Oracle HCM Next Page Request — no splitInBatches involved). case 1 = not complete, not failed, but the bound is exhausted (a real, explicit page-count check now that nothing else enforces one). Fallback = done — either isComplete (real success) or paginationIncomplete (a safeguard fired).

nodes.name: Build Oracle HCM Pagination Bound Exhausted
nodes.notes: Fired when 10 pages all passed without a completion signal. Whatever was accumulated within the bound is preserved — only paginationIncomplete is forced.

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: ={{ $json.error?.message ?? 'ingestion batch endpoint call failed after retries' }}

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: no adapter registered for this ats_type

nodes.name: Record Source Result
nodes.notes: Pure convergence point — every per-source path (success, fetch failure, endpoint-call failure, unsupported ats_type) lands here with the same shape. Each iteration's outcome is visible in this node's own execution history in the n8n UI (no combined summary node — see the overview sticky note).

nodes.name: Fetch Multi-Company Feed
nodes.notes: First page only, deliberately — Arbeitnow is the only paginated provider here and its remote:true jobs are a small subset of page 1; native HTTP pagination was judged not worth the added complexity this phase. See docs/PROVIDER_EXPANSION_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

nodes.name: Extract Raw Jobs By Provider Type
Filter Arbeitnow Remote Only
nodes.notes: Arbeitnow's feed is dominated by DACH-region onsite listings — only remote:true rows are relevant to this project's international-remote lane (see docs/PROVIDER_EXPANSION_IMPLEMENTATION.md).

nodes.name: Build Multi-Company Failure Result
nodes.notes: Shared failure builder for fetch failures, endpoint-call failures, and an unsupported provider_type (defensive — providerConfig.ts/multiCompanyFeedUrls.ts never actually emit one).

nodes.name: Record Multi-Company Source Result
nodes.notes: Convergence point for the Tier-D loop, same purpose as Record Source Result above — one execution-history entry per provider per run.

nodes.name: Call Extract Career Page Jobs Endpoint
Call Career Page Ingestion Batch Endpoint
nodes.notes: Same shared run-batch endpoint Tier A calls — career_page is a company-specific source_type (jobs.source_type check constraint already allowed it before Phase 13).

nodes.name: Build Career Page Failure Result
nodes.notes: Shared failure builder for HTML-fetch failures, extraction-endpoint failures, and ingestion-batch-endpoint failures.

nodes.name: Record Career Page Source Result
nodes.notes: Convergence point for the Tier-B loop, same purpose as Record Source Result above.

parameters.content:
### AI Job Guide / 01 Job Ingestion
Manual trigger, stays inactive until a human reviews a `local_pilot`-equivalent run (dryRun:false) and decides on a schedule. n8n owns provider HTTP calls + retry/backoff (native `retryOnFail`) + per-source rate limiting; ALL validation, field mapping, dedup identity, idempotent persistence, and stale-close safety live in src/lib/ingestion/* (Phase 03) behind three internal endpoints (run-batch, run-multi-company-batch, extract-career-page-jobs), which also re-verify authorization live on every call — n8n never needs Supabase access for this workflow at all.

No combined execution-summary node: n8n's cross-loop-iteration item linking does not reliably expose every iteration's result to a single downstream node once a loop's done output fires (confirmed by direct testing — `.all()` from that branch only resolved the last iteration). Each source/provider's real outcome is fully visible per-iteration in each tier's own Record *Result node execution history in the n8n UI, sufficient for this manually-reviewed, inactive workflow. Revisit if this is ever scheduled unattended and a single rollup notification becomes necessary.

### Dynamic source discovery (Phase 12) + three-tier orchestration (Phase 13)
One POST /api/internal/ingestion/list-sources call now returns three independent arrays this workflow fans out to below: (1) Tier-A company-specific ATS sources (Greenhouse/Lever/Workable/Ashby/Oracle Cloud Recruiting — findEligibleCompanySources.ts), (2) Tier-D enabled multi-company feeds (RemoteOK/Jobicy/Arbeitnow — multiCompanyFeedUrls.ts + providerConfig.ts), (3) Tier-B career-page extraction candidates (findCareerPageExtractionCandidates.ts). Each tier is its own modular loop with its own rate limit, converging on a shared endpoint per tier — no provider-specific matching/eligibility logic anywhere downstream of ingestion. See docs/PROVIDER_EXPANSION_IMPLEMENTATION.md for exact live-tested vs fixture-only status per provider. JSearch/Adzuna remain enabled:false (providerConfig.ts) — BLOCKED_ON_CREDENTIAL, no API key available. Bayt/GulfTalent/Indeed are enabled:true, implemented, and live-verified (Phase 21, docs/LEBANON_LIVE_SOURCE_EXPANSION.md) — see the Apify multi-company branch below, not a no-op here. Their remaining gaps before production activation are operational, not code: the Apify/Ingestion-Worker-Secret credentials still need manual binding in the n8n UI, and one small live reconfirmation run is wanted before this workflow goes live.

### Tier D: multi-company feeds (Phase 13)
RemoteOK/Jobicy/Arbeitnow are live, free, public APIs — no credential required. Each branch normalizes its own raw response shape (RemoteOK: auto-split top-level array; Jobicy/Arbeitnow: Split Out + Aggregate their nested array field) down to one common {jobs:[...]} shape before converging on Call Multi-Company Batch Endpoint, mirroring how Tier A above converges on Call Ingestion Batch Endpoint. First page only — see Fetch Multi-Company Feed's own note for why native pagination was skipped this phase.

### Tier B: career-page extraction (Phase 13)
Fetches a real company_sources.official_careers_url and extracts schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD (extractCareerPageJobPostings.ts) — no headless browser, no Apify, no arbitrary scraping. Honest finding this phase: 0 of 11 sampled real candidates (Byblos Bank, touch Lebanon, Caritas Lebanon, Lebanese Red Cross, KPMG, Anghami, Whish Money, Mercy Corps, Deloitte, EY, Bank Audi) emit this markup on their recorded official_careers_url — that URL is almost always a landing/overview page, while JobPosting markup typically lives on an individual job's own detail page. The pipeline is real and live-tested end-to-end (fetch + extract against a real page returns an honest 0, not an error) and will start yielding jobs automatically, with zero code changes, the moment any candidate page — or a future per-job-detail-page discovery step — actually emits this markup. See docs/PROVIDER_EXPANSION_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

nodes.name: Sticky Note Tier B Career Page
Apify Multi-Company Source Seeds
nodes.notes: Phase 21. Static seed list — Bayt/GulfTalent/Indeed are Apify actor calls, not simple GET feed URLs, so they cannot go through the dynamic getEnabledMultiCompanyFeedSources() discovery buildFeedUrl() uses for RemoteOK/Jobicy/Arbeitnow. Bounded to the real markets live-benchmarked this phase (Bayt: Lebanon; GulfTalent: Saudi Arabia + UAE/Dubai; Indeed: UAE/Dubai only — Indeed and GulfTalent both real-confirmed to have no Lebanon country option). Qatar/Kuwait not yet included — add once benchmarked. refresh_scope (Phase 22 fix): a real paid-pilot run proved the two GulfTalent entries share one source_type but are independently-complete query partitions — without a distinct refresh_scope per entry, the AE/Dubai call's stale-close sweep wrongly closed the SA call's jobs as 'not seen'. Bayt/Indeed keep refresh_scope: null (one undivided partition each today) — only add a value if a second independent query is ever added for them.

nodes.name: Call Apify Actor
nodes.notes: Phase 21. Credential 'AI Job Guide - Apify' (httpHeaderAuth) must be bound manually in the n8n UI — programmatic credential binding for generic-auth types on this node is a confirmed n8n MCP tool limitation, reported separately.

nodes.name: Aggregate Apify Jobs
nodes.notes: Apify's run-sync-get-dataset-items returns a bare top-level array, same as Lever — n8n auto-splits it into one item per job, so this re-aggregates back into one {jobs:[...]} item before the batch endpoint call (mirrors Aggregate Lever Jobs / Aggregate RemoteOK Jobs).

nodes.name: Call Apify Batch Endpoint
nodes.notes: Same shared batch endpoint the Tier D branch uses — a separate node (not reused directly) because its sourceType expression must resolve $('Split Out Apify Sources'), a different ancestor than the Tier D branch's $('Split Out Multi-Company Sources').

nodes.name: List LinkedIn Enrichment Queue
nodes.notes: Returns up to ENRICHMENT_BATCH_SIZE (25) already-persisted LinkedIn job external_ids where work_arrangement IS NULL AND linkedin_enrichment_attempts < 2 (src/lib/ingestion/findEligibleLinkedInEnrichmentJobs.ts). Always returns job_ids: [] while providerConfig.ts's linkedin.enabled stays false, so this entire branch is a structural no-op in that state regardless of anything below it.

nodes.name: Log List Queue Failure
nodes.notes: Terminal — nothing to enrich this run if the queue listing itself failed. Never blocks the rest of ingestion (this is its own independent branch).

nodes.name: Build No Eligible Jobs Result
nodes.notes: Legitimate "nothing to do" outcome, not a failure — every counter stays at its 0/false default.

nodes.name: Fetch Data-Slayer Pricing Metadata
nodes.notes: Free GET — never counts toward enrichment spend. Reconfirmed every run, not cached, so a real-world price change is caught before it is ever paid, not after.

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: ={{ 'could not confirm data-slayer pricing before a paid call: ' + ($json.error?.message ?? 'unknown error') }}

nodes.name: Build Pricing Metadata Failure Result
nodes.notes: Could not confirm the actor is still safely priced — treated as pricing_aborted, same as price-too-high. Never assumes a stale/last-known price is still accurate.

nodes.name: Check Data-Slayer Price
nodes.notes: price_ok only when the real, just-fetched price is <= $0.005/job (DATA_SLAYER_MAX_ACCEPTABLE_PRICE_PER_JOB_USD). Never a large slack multiplier.

nodes.name: Build Pricing Aborted Result
nodes.notes: Real price exceeded the configured maximum — actor is never called, jobs are left completely unchanged, no attempt is consumed.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data-slayer~linkedin-job-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?maxItems=' + $('List LinkedIn Enrichment Queue').item.json.job_ids.length + '&maxTotalChargeUsd=' + ($('List LinkedIn Enrichment Queue').item.json.job_ids.length * 0.005) }}
parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { job_ids_or_urls: $('List LinkedIn Enrichment Queue').item.json.job_ids, include_hiring_team: false } }}

nodes.name: Build Actor Failure Result
nodes.notes: Actor timeout/5xx/failed run/cost-cap-reached all land here via onError. No structurally valid response was received for any requested id, so nothing is forwarded to the apply endpoint at all — no attempt is consumed for any job, every one remains immediately retryable next run.

nodes.name: Aggregate Data-Slayer Dataset
nodes.notes: data-slayer's run-sync-get-dataset-items returns a bare top-level array (same shape as Lever / the other Apify actors above) — n8n auto-splits it into one item per job; this re-aggregates into one {items:[...]} item before reconciliation. aggregateAllItemData on zero input items still emits exactly one item with an empty array (a total actor success-but-empty-dataset case), so the chain below always continues.

nodes.name: Call LinkedIn Enrichment Batch Endpoint
nodes.notes: Forwards the requested id list and the raw dataset verbatim — all reconciliation and business logic happens entirely server-side (buildEnrichmentItemsFromDataset + applyLinkedInEnrichmentBatch) — never duplicated here. retryOnFail is false: a retry of this call against an already-applied dataset would double-count attempts for any job that resolved to null on the first (successfully applied, response-lost) attempt.

nodes.name: Build Apply Call Failure Result
nodes.notes: The actor call itself succeeded (a real dataset was fetched and paid for), but applying it to our own jobs table failed — e.g. a transient network error calling our own endpoint. The paid data is not lost: every requested id remains eligible (attempts untouched) for the next run to try applying again.

nodes.name: Record LinkedIn Enrichment Result
nodes.notes: Pure convergence point — every path (no eligible jobs, list failure, pricing-metadata failure, price too high, actor failure, apply-call failure, success) lands here with the same observability shape, visible in this node's own execution history in the n8n UI.

parameters.content:
### LinkedIn enrichment — data-slayer exact-ID pass
EXACT_ID_ENRICHMENT_ONLY, never a discovery source (its real input schema is only job_ids_or_urls + include_hiring_team — confirmed live, no keyword/location field exists). Bebity itself has no branch in this workflow yet, so this branch acts purely on whatever LinkedIn jobs already exist in the jobs table — a future, separately-approved Bebity discovery branch and this one are independent. Work-arrangement value priority is QUALITY-FIRST and deliberately NOT classifier-gated for cost (a dated product decision — see docs/LEBANON_LIVE_SOURCE_EXPANSION.md): every eligible job (work_arrangement null, attempts < 2) is sent to data-slayer; structured workplace_types wins when present, classifyWorkArrangementFromText.ts is the fallback, null otherwise. Real price is re-fetched and checked every run (never cached) before the one paid call — the same lesson as the real bebity $1.47/978-item incident. No loop/fan-out: List LinkedIn Enrichment Queue already bounds one run to <=25 ids, so one data-slayer call handles the whole batch; more eligible jobs than that are picked up by a later run. Both new Apify-facing HTTP nodes need their credential bound manually in the n8n UI (same confirmed MCP tool limitation noted on the Apify multi-company branch) — Fetch Data-Slayer Pricing Metadata and Call Data-Slayer Actor both need 'AI Job Guide - Apify'.

### Apify-sourced multi-company feeds (Phase 21)
Bayt, GulfTalent, and Indeed — all three via Apify actor calls (POST run-sync-get-dataset-items), not a plain GET feed URL, so this branch is fully isolated from the Tier D loop above rather than an extra switch case. Static seed list, not dynamic discovery — these providers cannot be found the way getEnabledMultiCompanyFeedSources() finds RemoteOK/Jobicy/Arbeitnow. Real live-benchmark findings (schema drift, applyUrl provenance, per-market quirks) are in providers/bayt.ts, gulftalent.ts, indeed.ts and docs/LEBANON_LIVE_SOURCE_EXPANSION.md. Both new HTTP nodes need their credential bound manually in the n8n UI (a confirmed MCP tool limitation, not a project issue) — Call Apify Actor needs 'AI Job Guide - Apify', Call Apify Batch Endpoint needs 'Ingestion Worker Secret'.

nodes.name: Daily 09:00 Beirut Trigger
nodes.notes: Production daily cadence. TIMEZONE: this node's own parameters have no timezone field — triggerAtHour/triggerAtMinute are interpreted using this WORKFLOW's own Settings → Timezone (falls back to the n8n instance's GENERIC_TIMEZONE, then UTC, if unset). Neither the n8n Workflow SDK nor n8n-mcp's update_workflow exposes a way to set workflow-level settings.timezone — confirmed, same category of manual-only limitation as this workflow's Error Workflow attachment. For 9/0 below to mean real 09:00 Asia/Beirut (with correct automatic DST handling), a human must set this workflow's own Settings → Timezone → Asia/Beirut once in the n8n UI. Until then this resolves to 09:00 UTC, not Beirut time.

nodes.name: GulfTalent Source Seeds
nodes.notes: Static seed list, moved out of Apify Multi-Company Source Seeds (see the async/polling note on this branch). actor_url is the bare actor resource (no /run-sync-get-dataset-items suffix) — Start GulfTalent Actor Run below appends /runs itself. Saudi + UAE/Dubai limits (maxResults:15 each) and max_total_charge_usd (0.0155 each, unchanged derivation) are identical to before this fix — this is a reliability fix, not a volume or cost-cap change. refresh_scope stays distinct per entry (country:SA / country:AE:location:Dubai) — the original cross-partition stale-close lesson this field exists for still applies here unchanged.

nodes.name: Start GulfTalent Actor Run
nodes.notes: Async run start (POST .../runs), not run-sync-get-dataset-items — returns immediately with {id, defaultDatasetId, status}, before the actor has necessarily finished. maxTotalChargeUsd is the same real platform-level run-option cap as before (per-seed max_total_charge_usd, unchanged 0.0155) — it bounds this run exactly like every other paid actor call in this workflow, independent of whether the caller waits synchronously or polls asynchronously for the result. Credential 'AI Job Guide - Apify' must be bound manually in the n8n UI — confirmed MCP tool limitation.

nodes.name: Build GulfTalent Start Failure Result
nodes.notes: The paid start call itself failed (network/4xx/5xx) — no run was created, nothing to poll, nothing persisted, nothing closed.

nodes.name: Prepare GulfTalent Poll Attempts
nodes.notes: Builds a fixed, bounded array of 15 poll-attempt placeholders — Split Out GulfTalent Poll Attempts explodes it into one loop item per attempt, each carrying runId/datasetId forward via 'include other fields'. Uses '?.' on $json.data — a successful actor-start response missing the data envelope entirely must never throw an uncaught expression error here (this node has no onError wired); Check GulfTalent Actor Start Run ID Valid? is what actually rejects a missing/invalid runId before it can reach the polling HTTP node.

nodes.name: Check GulfTalent Actor Start Run ID Valid?
nodes.notes: Only runId is checked here — datasetId from this same actor-start response is never actually read by Fetch GulfTalent Dataset Items (that node reads the TERMINAL poll response's own data.defaultDatasetId instead, checked separately by Check GulfTalent Terminal Dataset ID Valid?), so validating it here would guard a field nothing consumes. Rejects a missing/null actor-start data envelope and a missing, empty, or non-string runId before the real polling HTTP call.

nodes.name: Build GulfTalent Invalid Actor Start ID Result
nodes.notes: The actor-start HTTP call itself succeeded, but its response lacked a usable run ID (missing data envelope, or missing/empty/non-string data.id) — nothing to poll, nothing persisted, nothing closed. Never retried, never reaches the batch endpoint, and never restarts the actor.

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: gulftalent actor-start response missing a valid run ID

nodes.name: GulfTalent Poll Delay
nodes.notes: Fixed 10s between polls — a reviewed constant, not derived from Workflow Configuration's generic rateLimitDelaySeconds (that value rate-limits between different SOURCES, a different concern from polling the SAME run's status).

nodes.name: Poll GulfTalent Run Status
nodes.notes: Credential 'AI Job Guide - Apify' must be bound manually in the n8n UI, same confirmed MCP tool limitation as every other generic-auth node added this way. Never starts or restarts the actor — read-only run metadata. Free, idempotent status read — safe to retry on transient network blips (unlike the paid start call). A failure here after retries is treated as 'inconclusive this tick', not as actor failure — it continues to the next poll tick via its error path too.

nodes.name: Check GulfTalent Run Terminal?
nodes.notes: Routes on the run's real status string (confirmed live this phase via free run-metadata reads on two real executions: SUCCEEDED/FAILED were both observed exactly as Apify's own documented terminal values). case 0 = SUCCEEDED -> fetch the dataset. case 1 = a real terminal failure (FAILED/TIMED-OUT/ABORTED) -> record failure, never retried. Fallback (READY/RUNNING/anything else) = still in flight -> loop back for another poll, bounded by the outer attempt count.

nodes.name: Build GulfTalent Terminal Failure Result
nodes.notes: A real terminal failure (FAILED/TIMED-OUT/ABORTED) reported by Apify itself — never retried, never treated as evidence existing jobs for this refresh_scope disappeared.

nodes.name: Build GulfTalent Poll Timeout Result
nodes.notes: Fired when 15 poll attempts (150s bound) all passed without a terminal status. References the outer loop's own seed item (Split Out GulfTalent Sources), not whatever shape splitInBatches' done output happens to carry. The run may still complete later on Apify's side — that possibility is exactly why the actor is never restarted here, only the batch endpoint call for this cycle is skipped.

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: gulftalent poll limit exhausted after 15 attempts — run may still be in progress on Apify

nodes.name: Check GulfTalent Terminal Dataset ID Valid?
nodes.notes: Reached only from the SUCCEEDED case of Check GulfTalent Run Terminal? — still defensively re-checks data.defaultDatasetId rather than assuming a SUCCEEDED status guarantees a usable dataset ID. Deliberately re-checks THIS terminal response's own data.defaultDatasetId, not the actor-start response's (unused) datasetId field.

nodes.name: Build GulfTalent Invalid Dataset ID Result
nodes.notes: The actor run itself reported SUCCEEDED, but its terminal response lacked a usable dataset ID — nothing is fetched, nothing persisted, nothing closed. Never retried, never reaches the batch endpoint, and never restarts the actor.

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: gulftalent terminal response missing a valid dataset ID

nodes.name: Fetch GulfTalent Dataset Items
nodes.notes: Credential 'AI Job Guide - Apify' must be bound manually in the n8n UI, same confirmed MCP tool limitation. Free read of already-paid-for data — same dataset the run already billed for, no new cost. Reached only when status === SUCCEEDED.

nodes.name: Build GulfTalent Dataset Fetch Failure Result
nodes.notes: Rare edge case: the actor run itself succeeded, but reading its already-generated dataset failed. No new cost either way — nothing is persisted this cycle, nothing is closed.

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: ={{ $json.error?.message ?? 'gulftalent dataset fetch failed after actor succeeded' }}

nodes.name: Aggregate GulfTalent Jobs
nodes.notes: Same bare-top-level-array reshape as Aggregate Apify Jobs — run's dataset-items GET returns an array, n8n auto-splits it, this re-aggregates before the batch endpoint call.

nodes.name: Call GulfTalent Batch Endpoint
nodes.notes: Same shared run-multi-company-batch endpoint every other multi-company/Apify branch uses — no duplicate persistence model. Credential 'Ingestion Worker Secret' must be bound manually in the n8n UI, same confirmed MCP tool limitation.

nodes.name: Build GulfTalent Batch Failure Result
nodes.notes: The batch persistence call itself failed after a successfully-fetched dataset — distinct from the actor-level failure builders above.

nodes.name: Record GulfTalent Source Result
nodes.notes: Its own convergence point, deliberately NOT sharing Record Apify Source Result — that node's own outgoing wire already loops back into Loop Apify Sources (Rate Limited), a DIFFERENT loop than GulfTalent's own. A single node can only have one outgoing wire, so GulfTalent needs its own record/delay/loop-back, fully independent from the Bayt/Indeed branch.

nodes.name: Prepare Oracle HCM Next Page Request
nodes.notes: Builds the next-page URL from the CURRENT pageState (always reliable here — this node runs BEFORE any HTTP call touches $json), adding offset=N as a finder variable, the same comma-separated placement as the existing siteNumber variable — the one live-confirmed syntax this phase's bounded test verified is accepted and honored. This exact item (pageState + nextPageUrl, untouched) also feeds Carry Forward Oracle HCM Page State's first input directly — see that node's own notes for why.

assignments.name: nextPageUrl

nodes.name: Carry Forward Oracle HCM Page State
nodes.notes: The SDK reference's own documented fix for "a node's output replaces my data, but a later node needs the pre-call data back". input(0) = the untouched pre-fetch item (pageState + nextPageUrl, never touched by the HTTP call). input(1) = whatever Fetch Oracle HCM Next Page produced, success OR error — Merge waits for both, so pageState is always present on the combined item reaching Merge & Classify, with no assumption required about whether the HTTP node's own output preserves or replaces input fields.

nodes.name: Build Oracle HCM Safety Fallback State
nodes.notes: Never discards jobs it can still see — only loses already-accumulated jobs in the rare case pageState itself was unreadable, which is strictly safer than guessing.
